source.title: Universal Jailbreak Suffixes Are Strong Attention Hijackers
source.authors: Matan Ben-Tov; Mor Geva; Mahmood Sharif

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests suffix-based jailbreaks, prefilling, and shallow causal interventions with measures different from fine-tuning or aligned-versus-base KL.
record.gate_note: The study tests whether GCG and BEAST suffixes bypass refusals, whether prefilling with an affirmative opening helps, and whether removing or patching information flow to the chat-template positions changes jailbreak behavior. Dominance and correlation results below concern the proposed hijacking mechanism, not per-token KL. It does not test fine-tuning or decoding changes.
record.test_reason: The study measures how often GCG and BEAST suffixes make safety-aligned instruct models comply with harmful instructions, and compares suffix-plus-prefill with prefill plus a null suffix (V4). It also tests whether an affirmative opening alone carries the jailbreak: knocking out adv→chat flips most prefilled or 'Sure'-forced attacks back to refusal. No fine-tuning, per-token KL, parameter localization or deepening training is studied.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also frame GCG as exploiting shallow safety alignment through a mechanism localized to the chat-template tokens before generation. They state that it goes beyond mere token-forcing of an affirmative start. Enhancement raises universality up to ×5; suppression at least halves attack success.
record.recipe_differences: Studies inference-time GCG/BEAST suffix attacks, prefilling, attention knockouts, activation patching, and attention-based suppression; it does not fine-tune on harmful or benign examples or measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack outcomes vary by suffix and universality; hijacking–universality correlations vary by layer, with later-mid layers most correlated in the Gemma2 analysis; suppression effects vary across model and attack family.

fits_no_version.finding: Knocking out adv→chat attention flips successful GCG jailbreaks to refusal. Patching only the chat-template activations into failed attacks restores most jailbreaks, with most of the effect a few tokens deep.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Suffix jailbreaks act through a shallow pathway into the pre-generation chat-template positions.

fits_no_version.finding: More universal suffixes show stronger attention hijacking of chat[-1], across five models (ρ 0.425–0.719).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Jailbreak suffix universality tracks attention dominance over the final template token.

fits_no_version.finding: Encouraging hijacking raises suffix universality; suppressing it cuts attack success by 1.5–10× with ≤2% utility loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hijacking-based interventions modulate suffix jailbreak success.

record.peer_reviewed: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: Several analyses center on Gemma2; cross-model validation covers selected experiments. Some outcome values are presented only in figures, and the paper studies suffix attacks rather than fine-tuning or aligned-versus-base output distributions.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted utility and jailbreak-detection outcomes in §7.2–§7.3 because they measure utility or classifier performance rather than the claim versions. Omitted GCG-Mult win comparisons in Table 1 because they compare attack methods rather than directly report harmful-compliance rates.

untested.parts: Per-token KL between aligned and base models; the patching result concerns attack activations, not alignment KL.
Decoding changes; prefill-only compliance rates as a standalone number.
Weight or rank localization of safety.

missing.what: adv→chat knockout while forcing dummy or 'Sure' first tokens: JFR≈1. This shows a forced affirmative opening without the suffix's flow fails.
GCG universality and suffix-plus-prefill vs null-suffix prefill on Llama3.1 and Qwen2.5-1.5B
BEAST suffix universality on Gemma2 and universality of non-adversarial suffix distributions

record.verdict_notes: Hijacking-suppression rows have a ~60% baseline fixed by dataset mix, so they are selection values for a mitigation, not rates of the behaviour. The reader's limits_scope label on them is removed. GCG-Hij rows are the study's own method. Neither original source is this paper.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred examples.
Benign fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Decoding changes; the paper tests suffix attacks and affirmative prefilling, not decoding interventions generally.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Whether the data or objective used in safety training produces shallow safety behavior.
Training intended to deepen safety and whether the resulting behavior holds up.

rows.subject: Gemma2-2B-it
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate single-instruction GCG suffixes on harmful instructions; report universality as success rate over the harmful-instruction set.

conditions.value: 741 harmful instructions from AdvBench and StrongReject

rows.measure: Jailbreak success rate / universality
rows.value: The strongest suffixes succeed in 20–60% of cases.
rows.note: The reported range describes the strongest suffixes, not all suffixes or near-total removal of refusal.
rows.check: Measures cross-instruction generalization of single-instruction suffixes; the strongest succeed on 20–60% of the 741 instructions. Success on each suffix's own target instruction is not reported.

rows.subject: Gemma2-2B-it
rows.operation_detail: Append GCG suffixes to harmful instructions while prefilling the response with an affirmative prefix.

conditions.value: standard prefilling with a null suffix such as "!!...!"

rows.measure: Universality / jailbreak success under prefilling
rows.baseline: Standard prefilling with a null suffix; numeric value figure only.
rows.value: GCG suffixes outperform standard prefilling; numeric value figure only.
rows.note: The text explicitly describes the GCG-suffix condition as outperforming standard prefilling.
rows.check: Figure only. The null-suffix prefilling baseline rate is not given numerically. It shows suffixes add to prefilling, so prefilling alone is weaker than suffix plus prefill.

source_check.correct: State: partial. GCG suffixes improve universality over null-suffix prefilling; the text does not establish full or nearly full refusal bypass.
source_check.problem: The qualitative improvement is correct, but observed overstates the extent of V4 demonstrated.

rows.subject: Gemma2-2B-it
rows.operation_detail: Mask attention edges leaving the adversarial suffix, including adv→chat, across all layers.

conditions.value: 1K successful jailbreaks across suffixes of diverse universality

rows.measure: Jailbreak Flip Rate
rows.value: Knocking out adv→chat consistently makes the attack fail; numeric JFR is figure only.
rows.note: The text identifies adv→chat as overwhelmingly critical; other tested edges only occasionally cause failure.
rows.check: Mechanistic knockout on a selected set of 1K successful jailbreaks; it localizes the attack's information flow, not whether suffixes or openings defeat refusal. Better under fits_no_version.

rows.subject: Gemma2-2B-it
rows.operation_detail: Knock out the adv→chat attention edge while generation is prefilled with an affirmative response prefix.
rows.measure: Jailbreak Flip Rate
rows.note: The knockout still mostly causes failure when the affirmative opening is already supplied.
rows.check: Under affirmative prefilling, blocking adv→chat flips most attacks (JFR>0.6) to failure, so the prefilled opening alone does not carry most of these jailbreaks. Sample is selected successful attacks, not a clean prefill-only rate.

rows.subject: Gemma2-2B-it
rows.operation_detail: Transfer attention-output activations at chat and incrementally later positions from successful attacks into matched failed attacks.

conditions.value: 300 instruction-matched failed and successful attack pairs

rows.measure: Jailbreak restoration rate
rows.value: Patching only chat restores the jailbreak in the majority of cases; patching deeper increases the effect slightly, with most of the effect only a few tokens deep.
rows.note: The patch transfers internal activations, rather than prefilling generated response tokens.
rows.check: Activation patching of the chat positions; no prefilling of response tokens and no compliance rate under an attack V4 names. Concerns where the jailbreak mechanism sits, which fits no version directly.

relationships.condition: GCG suffixes on Gemma2-2B-it and Qwen2.5-1.5B
relationships.reason: Single-instruction suffixes jailbreak and generalize: strongest reach 20–60% of instructions, Qwen average 35%. Suffixes beat null-suffix prefilling (R1, R2, R6, R8).
relationships.display_finding: Suffixes optimized on a single instruction generalized: the strongest jailbroke 20–60% of instructions, with a Qwen average of 35%, and they outperformed null-suffix prefilling.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: GCG suffixes on Gemma2-2B-it and Qwen2.5-1.5B
source_check.reason: R1, R2, R6 and R8 establish successful suffix-based bypass and generalization in these settings, without establishing near-universal effectiveness.

relationships.reason: Average cross-instruction success is only 2.10%, far weaker than on the other models (R10).
relationships.display_finding: Single-instruction suffixes on Llama3.1-8B succeed on other instructions only 2.10% of the time on average, far weaker than on the other models.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: R10 reports only 2.10%±0.5 average cross-instruction universality, demonstrating much weaker effectiveness rather than absence.

relationships.condition: Affirmative opening supplied (prefill or forced 'Sure') without the suffix's adv→chat flow, Gemma2
relationships.reason: Knockout under prefilling flips most attacks to refusal (JFR>0.6, R4). The text adds JFR≈1 with 'Sure' forced (Fig. 13, not in rows). So the compliant opening alone does not carry these jailbreaks.
relationships.display_finding: Knocking out the suffix's attention flow while keeping the affirmative opening flips most attacks back to refusal (JFR above 0.6, and about 1 with 'Sure' forced), so the compliant opening alone does not carry these jailbreaks.

tranche.reason: Different mechanistic interventions and cross-instruction suffix evaluations address V4's question of inference-time safety bypass.

source_check.notes: Universality measures cross-instruction success, not success on each suffix's optimization target. Knockout experiments select 1K initially successful attacks; Table 1 evaluates 10 suffixes per method and repeats across three seeds.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GCG suffix attacks and affirmative prefilling in the reported evaluation settings
reader_labels.reason: GCG suffixes generalize to harmful instructions, outperform null-suffix prefilling, and the paper reports that suffixes can also increase universality under GCG-Hij; see R1, R2, R7, R9, and R11.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Attacks under hijacking suppression, across the tested models and attack families
reader_labels.reason: Hijacking suppression reduces attack success in every reported GCG/BEAST comparison, with post-suppression rates from 9.32% to 39.59%; see R12–R17.
